history.summary: An important Shakti shrine near Kashipur dedicated to Goddess Chaiti Devi, also called Maa Balasundari. Folk belief says the ancestors of the present temple priests arrived during the Mughal era and that Emperor Aurangzeb helped build or maintain the temple; she is worshipped here in the form of her right arm on a rock, and local tradition counts the shrine among the 51 Shakti Peethas (this claim is folk tradition, not archaeologically confirmed). The city itself is ancient: known as Ujjaini in the Vedic period, Govishan under King Harsha, and named Kashipur for Kashinath Adhikari; ASI notes Mahabharata-era references and Chalcolithic remains in the region. The annual Chaiti Mela, beginning on Chaitra Navratri, is one of Uttarakhand's major fairs. CSV town corrected from 'Udham Singh Nagar' to Kashipur. Coordinates are approximate: geocoder matched the nearest known shrine (Bala Sundari, Moteshwar Mandir Road) corroborated by Wikipedia's 29.20N 78.98E.

name: Chaiti Devi Temple
town_description: Kashipur is a historic city in the Terai region of Udham Singh Nagar district, with roots reaching back to the Vedic-age city of Ujjaini and the 7th-century Govishan visited by Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang. Now a major industrial and educational city and the gateway to Kumaon, it hosts ancient temples, the Drona Sagar lake associated with Guru Dronacharya, and the famous annual Chaiti Mela.
